findings.evidence: Archiving "Q3 Roadmap" will remove it from the active projects list for everyone on the team. You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list.
findings.violation: This confirmation promises the archived project can be restored at any time from the archived projects list, but no state named or resembling an archived projects list is defined anywhere in the artifact, so the reversal path the artifact itself claims has no route a user can actually take within the design as specified.
findings.fix: Define the archived projects list as a reachable state, for example linked from the workspace overview or project settings, with a restore control on each archived project, or remove the restore claim from the confirmation copy if no such list exists.

findings.violation: The artifact specifies a state-changing commit control but names no confirmation message, success or failure indication, or next state that follows it, so a user who clicks it cannot tell from the artifact whether the change took effect.
findings.fix: Specify what the user sees after this control is used: a confirmation message in place, a changed control state, or a defined next screen.

findings.location: the "project-settings" section, the "Back to your projects" link
findings.evidence: the "project-settings" section defines a "Save" button and, separately, a "Back to your projects" link, with no text stating what becomes of an edited but unsaved project name if the link is used instead of the button.
findings.violation: This screen lets the user edit the project name field but the artifact never states what becomes of an edited, unsaved value if the user takes the Back to your projects exit instead of Save, so the exit does not clearly cost the user nothing already entered.
findings.fix: State explicitly what happens to unsaved edits when this exit is used, for example a confirm-discard prompt, or note that edits are saved automatically so the exit is safe.

findings.location: the "invite-member" section, the "Save" button and the "Continue" link
findings.violation: Two distinct controls appear on this screen for what reads as one task, sending an invite: a form Save button and a separate Continue link that leads to the invite sent state. The artifact gives no cue whether Save and Continue perform the same action, or what Save alone does, so a user cannot tell which control actually sends the invite.
findings.fix: Remove the redundant control, or state what each does, for example relabel the form submit Send invite and drop the separate Continue link, or explain that Save stores a draft while Continue sends it.

findings.evidence: An invite was sent to the address entered above. It expires in 5 days if not accepted.
findings.violation: The confirmation text refers to the address entered above, but the address was entered on the previous invite-member state, not on this state, and this state never displays the actual email address, so the reference is inaccurate for where the user is now and the user cannot verify which address the invite went to without returning to the prior screen.
findings.fix: State the actual email address entered, for example An invite was sent to jane@example.com, so the user can verify it without leaving this screen.

findings.evidence: The last import finished with 4 rows skipped: each referenced a project that does not exist in this workspace. Rows 35, 71, 78, and 83 were skipped; every other row was imported.
findings.violation: This state explains that 4 rows were skipped and why, but the only control it offers is Back to your projects; the artifact provides no way to retry the skipped rows, create the missing referenced projects, or otherwise act on the 4 specific failures from this state.
findings.fix: Add a direct recovery action from this state, for example a link to re-run the import for the 4 skipped rows, or a link to create the missing referenced projects named in the skipped rows.
